fieldValues.title: Text-anchor injection can silently spill into an unrelated composition
fieldValues.summary: A Node-side post-render text splice that anchors on a heading's literal text, rather than scoping to the specific view(s) it targets, matches that heading wherever it recurs across every rendered composition -- and neither the release-drift check nor the publish-completeness guard would have caught it.
evidence: invariant-region.mjs's injectKeyInvariants originally anchored on the literal text 'Key Invariants', unique across every VIEW_EXPORTS composition only by accident -- exactly two views (srs-spec.md, srs-unified.md) ever authored that heading, via a section record only those compositions' container-subset sourcing reached.

srs#710 (RFC-042 Change B) required redesigning the anchor to 'Validation' once the Key Invariants record was deleted. 'Validation' is not similarly unique: srs-glossary.md's concept-glossary composition also renders a 'Validation' entry (concepts listed alphabetically).

A first-draft fix called injectKeyInvariants unconditionally over every VIEW_EXPORTS entry, exactly as the old code always had (relying on 'null' return + requiresKeyInvariants to gate side effects). Running publish-spec.mjs with that draft spliced a spurious '### Key Invariants' block (319 lines) into docs/spec/srs-glossary.md, alphabetically misplaced (inserted at 'Validation's position, not 'Key' order).

check-release-drift.mjs did not catch it: publish-spec.mjs is the generator, so after it runs, the committed file trivially 'matches' whatever it just wrote, correct or not -- the drift check is only meaningful against a prior, independently-produced baseline.

checkPublishCompleteness (scripts/lib/publish-completeness.mjs, srs#396) did not catch it either: it verifies every renderer-emitted heading survives into the committed export (nothing lost), but has no corresponding check that no extra heading was spuriously added.
Caught only by manually reading `git status`/`git diff docs/` after the first publish-spec.mjs run, before committing -- not by any automated gate.

Fix: scope both call sites (publish-spec.mjs's injectInvariants, check-release-drift.mjs's applyInvariantInjection) to entry.requiresKeyInvariants explicitly, rather than relying on the anchor text's incidental global uniqueness. Verified live by reverting the scoping in check-release-drift.mjs alone and re-running it: FAILED: rendered document drift: .../srs-glossary.md is stale -- re-render to update (exit 1); reverted, re-ran green (exit 0).
fieldValues.body:
## The general lesson

Any Node-side text-splice mechanism that locates its insertion point by matching literal rendered text (a heading, a marker string) against a *shared pool* of rendered outputs must scope which outputs it may touch explicitly -- by view id, by a `requiresX`-style flag, whatever the codebase's existing idiom is -- rather than applying itself to every output and trusting a `null`/no-match return to make it a no-op elsewhere. Uniqueness of the anchor text across all current outputs is not a property that survives refactoring; the moment the anchor changes (as this unit had to change it, since the record that authored the old anchor text was retired), an anchor that used to be incidentally unique can become ambiguous, and the mechanism silently starts touching outputs it was never meant to.

## The gap this exposed

Neither of this repository's two rendered-docs guards would have caught this class of defect:

- `check-release-drift.mjs` compares the *committed* file against a *freshly rendered-and-injected temp copy* -- but only after `publish-spec.mjs` (the generator) has already been run once and has already overwritten the committed file with its own (possibly wrong) output. It proves internal self-consistency of one run, never correctness against an independent baseline.
- `checkPublishCompleteness` (srs#396) is a one-directional guard: every heading the CLI's raw render emits must survive into the committed export. It has no inverse check that every heading in the committed export was actually emitted by the raw render (i.e. that nothing was added that the renderer never produced). A spurious insertion by the *Node-side* injection step, downstream of the CLI's own raw render, is exactly the case this asymmetry misses.

This finding does not propose closing that gap within srs#710's scope (a general spurious-heading guard is a separate, larger design question -- what counts as "spurious" for a mechanism that legitimately does add generated content, like this one, needs its own affirmative test rather than a blanket prohibition). It is recorded so whoever next touches this rendering pipeline, or designs a similar text-splice mechanism elsewhere in the codebase, knows this exact failure mode was hit once already and was caught by luck (a reviewer reading a diff) rather than by any gate.
